D005-D007_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling for about two months now—maybe a bit longer. Everything started with this heavy dread, like something terrible is coming. I keep thinking the world is on the verge of collapsing—not like a normal worry, but a certainty. I don’t know how to explain it, but I *know* something is about to end. Sometimes, I see shadows in my apartment when I’m alone, figures standing in the corners, but when I turn on the light, nothing’s there. Once, I saw my husband’s face change—like it wasn’t him anymore. I didn’t say anything because I was scared he’d think I’m losing it.

I used to love my design work—sketching interfaces, solving problems—but now I can’t focus. Deadlines pile up, and I just sit there, overwhelmed. I don’t enjoy anything anymore, not even things we used to do together. I cry a lot, feel numb. There are days I don’t get out of bed. But I can’t tell how long I’ve felt this sad—some days are worse, some are... just empty. I don’t know if the darkness I see is outside me or inside.
D005-D007_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D007_h001.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about two months now, maybe a bit more. At first, it was just this taste—like copper or blood—whenever I’d eat, even when I wasn’t eating at all. I’d rinse my mouth, brush, nothing helped. Then I started noticing things… like my neighbors watching me too much when I deliver mail, even on days I’m not working. I know I’m a postman, so people see me around, but it feels different now. I think someone’s putting something in my food. I can still taste it, you know? Not all the time, but enough.

My wife says I’ve been down, not sleeping right, not enjoying things. I worry about the job—I’ve been doing it for 25 years—but lately I just feel heavy, like I’m dragging myself through the day. I don’t know if it’s the stress or if something’s really after me. There are days when the sadness lifts a little, but the thoughts don’t go away. I can’t tell if the bitterness in my mouth is real or if it’s in my head. It’s been like this on and off, but I can’t pin down when the low moods started compared to the other stuff—it’s all just tangled.
D005-D007_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D007_h002.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h003.question:
Lately, things have felt… off. For about two months now, I’ve been tasting things that aren’t there—like metal, or something spoiled, even when I haven’t eaten anything. At first I thought it was my food, but it happens all the time, even first thing in the morning. I’ve started to worry there’s something really wrong inside me—like my liver’s failing or there’s a tumor nobody’s found. The doctors have run tests, but they say everything’s fine. I don’t know who to believe. 

I’ve also just… feel heavy, y’know? Like I can’t get out from under this fog. I still go to work, keep things moving at the warehouse, but it takes everything just to show up. My wife says I’ve been quiet, distant. She’s right. I don’t enjoy much anymore, not even the things I used to. Some days, I don’t even want to get out of bed. But I do. I have to. I can't say how long the low mood lasts—some days better, some worse. And those tastes, the worries about my body—they don’t seem to ever really go away.

A. Schizophrenia

    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h004.question:
I’ve been struggling for about two months now—maybe a bit more, I’ve lost track. At first, it was just this sour, metallic taste that wouldn’t go away, no matter what I ate. I rinsed, brushed, even stopped drinking coffee—nothing helped. Then I started tasting things like rotten eggs, even when I wasn’t eating anything. The worst part is, I know it’s not real, but it *feels* real.  

Lately, I can’t shake this certainty that everything’s falling apart—that the systems are failing, not just code, but the world. Like, the servers are down for good, and no one’s fixing them because it’s already over. I know how that sounds, but it’s not just a feeling. It’s like I *know* it’s happening. I can’t focus at work, and my team’s starting to notice. I used to find bugs in minutes; now I just sit there, staring at the screen, wondering if it even matters.  

I’ve been down lately, yeah—can’t sleep, lost my appetite, don’t care about anything. It’s hard to tell what’s from the stress and what’s… something else. Some days the thoughts are loud, others not as much, but the taste? That’s always there. And there are times—short bursts—where I feel okay, almost normal, but they don’t last.
D005-D007_h004.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D007_h004.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h005.question:

Sometimes it’s just murmurs, other times it sounds like a customer—specifically one man who dines alone on Thursdays. I’ve been down lately, too. Waking up exhausted, even after sleep. I don’t laugh with my husband like I used to, and some mornings I just sit in the office staring at the wall. And then there are days when both feel unbearable. I can’t tell if I’m just overworked or if something in my mind has truly changed.

A. Schizophrenia

    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h006.question:
I’ve been off for about seven months now—maybe a bit more. Things just don’t feel real sometimes. I keep thinking something’s wrong inside me, like my heart’s rotting or my liver’s shutting down, even though all the tests come back clean. The doctors say I’m fine, but I *know* something’s happening in there.  

I’ve noticed myself repeating things people say—like an echo. My wife pointed it out first. I didn’t even realize I was doing it until she got upset. It just slips out.

There are times I feel a little worse, emotionally—low, drained, like I’m dragging myself through each day. But I can’t say how long that’s been going on compared to the other stuff. It’s hard to tell what’s what.

    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h007.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about seven months—like my body isn’t really mine. I keep thinking something’s wrong inside, like my organs are shifting or not working the way they should, even though all my checkups come back normal. I can’t shake it, no matter how many times the doctors say I’m fine.  

There are moments, usually when I’m alone after class, where I just freeze—arms raised or bent in a pose, like I’m still teaching—but I don’t feel like I can move. It’s not intentional. I used to love sharing energy with my students, but now I feel flat. I don’t cry or get angry—I just… don’t show anything. My voice sounds dull even to me. I’ve lost interest in things, sure, and some days I can’t get out of bed, but I can’t tell if that’s from the sadness or just the numbness. It’s all blended together. I’ve had low moods on and off, but I don’t know if they’ve been there long enough—or strongly enough—to mean anything.

A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h008.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for about the last seven months. Things started shifting at work—small things at first. I’m a veterinarian, so I’m used to being focused, but I found myself getting distracted, not speaking much during staff meetings, even when asked directly. I just didn’t feel the need to say much. My technician asked if I was okay, and all I could manage was “Yeah,” even though I wasn’t sure that was true.

There’s this woman—my clinic’s radiologist. She doesn’t know me well, but I’m certain she’s been sending me signals. Little smiles, how she tucks her hair when she walks by. I know it sounds strange, but I feel like she’s in love with me. I haven’t told her, of course. I don’t want to scare her, but I think she’s waiting for me to make a move. I find myself rearranging my schedule just to cross paths with her.

Lately, I’ve felt heavy, like I’m moving through water. I don’t enjoy things like I used to—not the job, not even my dog. Some days I just sit. I can’t explain it. I don’t know if it’s sadness or just… emptiness. It’s hard to tell anymore.
D005-D007_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D007_h008.answer: D & A. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h009.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about seven months now—maybe longer, but that’s when things started messing with my head. Driving the rig used to give me peace, just me and the road, but now I can’t shake this idea that my ex is seeing someone else. We’ve been divorced two years, but I keep thinking she’s with that guy from her job, even though I’ve got no proof. I tell myself I shouldn’t care, but it eats at me.

Sometimes, when I stop for the night, I’ll sit in the cab in this stiff position, arms out like I’m holding the wheel, even when I’m not. I don’t plan it—it just happens.     C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h010.question:
I’ve been working nights at the warehouse for twelve years now—used to be quiet, predictable. But about seven months ago, things started feeling… off. I’d hear the distant hum of the freeway, or coworkers talking in the break room, and I’d swear they were sending me messages. Not just idle talk—like coded instructions meant for me. Even the way people move their hands when they speak… sometimes I catch myself mimicking it, my arms sort of staying where they’re placed, like they’re heavy. It’s not on purpose.

Talking feels harder now. Not that I have much to say lately—just feels like my thoughts run thin. I used to call my daughter every Sunday. Haven’t in weeks. Don’t know what to tell her. Honestly, most days I can’t get out of bed until it’s time to clock in. I’m tired all the time, and nothing seems to matter. But it’s not just sadness—it’s like the world’s muffled, even when I hear things too clearly. 

There have been times, maybe a day or two, where the low mood lifted a little, but the thoughts about the messages—they never really go away. I can’t say exactly how long any of it lasts. It all just… blends together.

A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about four months now—can’t quite shake it. Lately, I keep thinking my wife is seeing someone else, even though I’ve got no real proof. She’s been with me since the garage days, and she’s always been steady, but I just… I can’t help it. I watch her phone when she’s not looking. She says I’m acting strange, and maybe I am. Sometimes I pace the apartment, back and forth by the kitchen window—my arms swing a certain way, like they’re moving on their own. My coworker mentioned it last week, said I was doing it during break.

I don’t feel like myself. I used to take pride in keeping things clean, doing an honest day’s work, but now I drag. Some mornings I don’t want to get up. No joy in much. But is it the sadness driving the thoughts, or the thoughts feeding the sadness? Hard to tell. There were a couple of days last month I felt a bit clearer, but not long enough to believe it meant anything. I just keep moving, keep checking, keep walking the same line in the linoleum.

A. Specific Phobia
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h012.question:

A doctor will make a passing comment, or a nurse laughs in the hallway, and I’m sure it’s about me—like there’s a hidden message. I’ve noticed myself making odd faces—my jaw tightens, or I pull a strange expression without meaning to. My husband mentioned it the other day, and I didn’t even realize I was doing it. It’s embarrassing.

Honestly, I’m just tired—mentally drained. I don’t enjoy things like I used to, even little moments with my husband. Some days I feel hopeless, like I’m failing at everything. But I can’t say if the mood came first or the… the thoughts. And whether the low mood has been there most of the time? I don’t know. It comes and goes.     D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h013.question:

It’s not that I don’t care; it’s like something inside just… shuts down. My husband tries to help, but I’ve started noticing little things—how he texts his colleague late at night, the way he changes clothes after class. I know he says it’s nothing, but I *feel* it—there’s a connection I’m not supposed to see. He wouldn’t lie, would he?

Some days I don’t get out of bed. Not because I’m sad exactly, but because moving feels pointless. My department head asked me to lead a seminar last month, and I just stared at her, didn’t say anything. I didn’t mean to be rude—I was stuck. Even now, when my wife speaks to me, sometimes I don’t answer. Not out of anger. It’s like my mind stops cooperating.

I used to love teaching, but now I sit in my office and feel empty. I don’t know how long this low mood’s been here—weeks? Months? It blurs with the other thoughts. There are times—maybe a week or so—when the sadness lifts a little, but the suspicion stays.

D005-D007_h014.question:

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h015.question:

D005-D007_h016.question:

D005-D007_h017.question:

D005-D007_h018.question:
I’ve been off for about three months now—my wife’s been on me about it, saying I don’t talk like I used to, like I’m somewhere else. At first, I thought maybe it was just stress from the job, but then things started feeling… different. I’d be on site, hard hat on, and swear I could feel ants crawling under my skin, even after I’d shower. Nothing’s there, but I can *feel* it.

I try to explain things to my crew, but words get tangled. One minute I’m talking safety, the next I’m thinking about the stars and how they’re sending signals. My boss pulled me aside—he said I’m not connecting like before. I guess… I don’t laugh much. Don’t feel the need. 

I haven’t been sleeping well. Sometimes I wonder if I’m depressed, but honestly, I can’t tell if I’m sad or just… tuned in to something bigger. It’s not constant, though. There are days—maybe a week here and there—where none of that stuff comes up, but then it drifts back.

A. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h019.question:
I’ve been off for about three months now—maybe a bit more, I’ve lost track. There are days when things just don’t connect right. I hear voices, mostly women, whispering that they understand me, that someone important—someone famous, actually—has been sending me signals through the radio. D005-D007_h020.question:

Then it started feeling like I was different in a special way—like I was meant for something bigger, meant to uncover truths others couldn’t see. A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h021.question:
I’ve been working at the library for over thirty years—quiet, predictable, just the way I like it. But lately, things have felt… different. For the past few months, I’ve started noticing figures in the stacks—people who aren’t there. Just out of the corner of my eye, someone in a long coat or a woman with a red hat, but when I turn, no one’s there.  

And honestly, I’ve begun to wonder—maybe I’m not just a librarian. I’ve had moments where I feel like I’m meant for something far greater, like I’ve been chosen to uncover hidden knowledge, something no one else can see. Sometimes I write notes in code, convinced it’s important, though I can’t explain why.  

But with all that, I haven’t felt like myself. Low, tired, like the joy’s been drained out. I still go to work, but I don’t answer when people talk to me—sometimes I just can’t bring myself to respond, even if I want to.  

The sadness comes and goes, I suppose. I don’t know if it’s been most of the time—hard to say. And those visions or thoughts… I can’t tell if they’re signs of truth or just broken pieces. I can’t recall ever having two weeks where the odd thoughts stayed without the heaviness—everything just… blurs together.
